what_worked: Three-lever stacking analysis is genuinely original synthesis; causal discipline and limitations are exemplary throughout.
fix_next: Several figures (category missing count 27% vs 274/1000=27.4%, AI revenue share 15%, cohort percentages) are unverifiable or slightly off—show denominators explicitly.
verdict: Rigorous, well-narrated, insight-rich deck with minor accuracy gaps.
factual_error_detail: Slide 6: 'Sales' category ($986 median) appears in chart but is not in the reference dataset categories—possibly fabricated or mislabeled. Slide 6: AI captures '15% of revenue'—actual is ~16.3% ($2,356,676/$14,444,164 among categorized), minor but stated with false precision. Slide 4: 49.6% top-10 share matches reference exactly, but the 'mean is 39× the median' claim ($15,596 mean vs $400 median = 39×) checks out. Slide 2: Coverage gap for Category shown as 27%—actual is 274/1000=27.4%, acceptable rounding. The 'Sales' category inclusion is the clearest error.

evidence.insight: Slide 9's three-lever stacking (B2B + ARPU≥$50 + DR≥40 → 65× median lift) goes well beyond describing charts; the accelerating/flat/decaying cohort decomposition on slide 5 adds genuine analytical depth; the AI paradox framing on slide 6 is decision-useful.
evidence.narrative: Clear thesis stated on slide 1 (20% vs 80%), built through concentration → momentum → category → pricing → distribution → synthesis → recommendations → conclusion. Each insight feeds the next; the 'main story' slide (9) synthesizes all prior findings into one actionable framework. Strong landing on slide 11.
evidence.framing: Slide 2 explicitly states cross-sectional nature, coverage gaps with percentages, and what the file contains. Slide 3 lists all assumptions including exclusion of 32 inconsistent rows and 726-row category denominator. Slide 11 states four limitations including self-selection bias and association-not-causation. Audience (founders) is implicit but clear.
evidence.accuracy: Top-10 share (49.6%), zero-revenue count (216), total revenue ($15.6M), category medians (Education $2,435, Marketing $2,370, AI $503, Productivity $80) all match reference closely. However: 'Sales' category on slide 6 is not in the reference dataset. The SaaS median shown as $201 vs reference $200.50 is fine rounding. Content Creation $1,238 vs reference $1,237.50 is fine. The 27% category label matches reference 274 rows. The 'AI captures 15% of revenue' is approximate but slightly off.
evidence.visual: Consistent dark-red palette with clear hierarchy; bar charts are appropriately chosen and well-labeled with values. Slide 9's stepped bar chart effectively communicates the lever-stacking thesis. Coverage gap chart on slide 2 is smart. No chartjunk. Minor issue: slide 7's stacked bar could use clearer segment labeling. Overall restrained and evidence-led.
evidence.ai_slop: Minimal. The deck avoids generic consulting language; every claim is tied to specific numbers. The title slide's '20% who build businesses vs 80% who build projects' is slightly clickbaity but earned by the analysis. No decorative-but-meaningless graphics. No filler slides.
